_comment: The queuer's call order for one queue item, read off its configureOverlay and
section 2). `skipFor` / `onlyFor` mirror the queuer's own guards (isGen1 / isGen2 / isGen4),
so replaying this script for a genN fixture issues exactly the calls the queuer would issue.
The guards are the queuer's, not the overlays': it sends /set-starter, /set-evolution,
/refresh, /set-right-panel, /set-splits and /new-run to gen1 too, where the legacy app
had no server to answer (every one of those fails there) and the unified app answers.
The values are what the queuer sends for an item with no evolution, no split file and
the default hidden-power type; $expectedGame and $rightPanel are computed per fixture
the way the queuer computes them per item (tools/parity/control-script.ts). /set-game is
sent unconditionally here where the queuer sends it only when /status disagrees.
/quit is deliberately last and /reload is left out: both take the window away, and the
harness needs the app alive to finish the run. They are covered by their own scripts.
name: queuer-item

calls.comment: readiness poll: the queuer waits up to 120 s for ready:true
only on a mismatch in the queuer; the mapping is null for gen1
gen2: after the counters; gen4: before the evolution
gen4 sets the evolution after the refresh
gen1, gen3, gen5: before the refresh
